sanskrit: cittiṃ yajāmi manasā cittiṃ devām̐ ṛtāvṛdhaḥ | jātavedaḥ pra ṇas tira- -agne viśvābhir ūtibhiḥ ||
english: I worship Thought with my mind, the Thought of the gods who augment the cosmic order. O Jātavedas, O Agni, carry us across with all thy aids.

sanskrit: yāvayāsmad dveṣāṃsi yavamayena haviṣā | yas te trita duṣvapnyasya bhāgaḥ sa ta eṣa taṃ ta etaṃ pra hiṇmaḥ ||
english: Drive away enmities from us with the barley oblation. Whatever share of the evil dream belongs to thee, O Trita — that same do we here dispatch unto thee.

sanskrit: yathā kalāṃ yathā śaphaṃ yatharṇaṃ saṃnayanti | evā duṣvapnyaṃ sarvam apriye saṃ nayāmasi ||
english: As they bring together the kalā measure, as the hoof, as a debt — so do we gather together all evil-dreaming into the Unfavorable One.

sanskrit: araro hai śatam adya gavāṃ bhakṣīya śatam ajānāṃ śatam avīnāṃ śatam aśvānāṃ śataṃ puruṣāṇām | tatrāpi bhakṣīyāmum āmuṣyāyaṇam amuṣyāḥ putram ||
english: Ha, the glutton! Today let him consume a hundred cattle, a hundred goats, a hundred sheep, a hundred horses, a hundred men — and there too let him devour that one, yonder son of that man, that man's offspring.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ nirṛtaye pra yacchāmi taṃ mṛtyoḥ pāśe badhnāmi | sa baddho hato astu sa tato mā moci ||
english: Him do I hand over to Nirṛti; him do I bind in the noose of Mṛtyu. Bound and slain let him be; from there let him never be released.

sanskrit: ye naḥ śapanty apa te bhavantu vṛkṣān iva vṛkṇām̐ ati tām̐ ayāma | drāghīya āyuḥ prataraṃ dadhānā vayaṃ devānāṃ sumatau syāma ||
english: Those who curse us — let them be cut off; we shall pass beyond them as past felled trees. Bearing a longer, more extended life, may we abide in the good favour of the gods.

sanskrit: kṛtyākṛtaṃ praty avasānadarśanam agne prati sma budhyasva | prati sma deva taṃ daha ||
english: O Agni, be thou fully awake against the sorcerer who worked the kṛtyā-spell, him who looks toward destruction. O god, burn that one down.

sanskrit: yas tvā kṛtye prajighāya vidvām̐ aviduṣo gṛham | punas tvā tasmā ā dadhmo yathā kṛtyākṛtaṃ hanaḥ ||
english: He who knowingly launched thee, O kṛtyā-spell, against the house of an ignorant man — we place thee back upon that one, so that thou mayest smite the one who wrought the kṛtyā.

sanskrit: punaḥ kṛtyāṃ kṛtyākṛte hastagṛhya parā ṇaya | uto tam attu sā punas tarda iva sadanaṃ svam ||
english: Take the kṛtyā-spell by the hand and lead it back to its maker. Let it then devour him, and return again to its own dwelling, like a woodpecker.

sanskrit: kṛtyā yantu kṛtyākṛtaṃ vṛka ivāvimato gṛham | tokaṃ pākasya vardhatāṃ suvṛṣṭa oṣadhīr iva ||
english: Let the kṛtyā-spells go back to their maker, as a wolf to the house of one who lacks cattle. Let the offspring of the innocent flourish like herbs under good rain.

sanskrit: yat te grāvā bāhucyuto acucyon naro yad vā te hastayor adhukṣan | tat ta ā pyāyatāṃ tat te ni ṣṭyāyatāṃ soma rājan ||
english: What of thee was wrung out by the pressing-stone flung from the arm, what the men squeezed from thee into the hands — let that swell back for thee, let that stiffen again for thee, O king Soma.

sanskrit: yat te grāvṇā cicchiduḥ soma rājan priyāṇy aṅgā sukṛtā purūṇi | tat saṃ dhatsvājyenota vardhayasva- -anāgaso yathā sadam it saṃkṣiyema ||
english: What of thy dear and well-made limbs, many as they are, were cut asunder by the pressing-stone, O king Soma — join those together with ghee and grow strong, so that we, being without offence, may ever dwell in thee.

sanskrit: yāṃ te tvacaṃ bibhidur yāṃ ca yoniṃ yad vāsthānāt pracyuto yadi vā suto 'si | tvayā soma kl̥ptam asmākam etad upa no rājan sukṛte hvayasva ||
english: The skin of thee they split, and the matrix — whether thou wast dislodged from thy resting-place or art pressed out — what has been prepared for us by thee, O Soma, O king, call us in that good deed.

sanskrit: saṃ prāṇāpānābhyāṃ sam u cakṣuṣā saṃ śrotreṇa gacchasva soma rājan | yat te viriṣṭaṃ sam u tat ta etaj jānītān naḥ saṃgamane pathīnām ||
english: Come together with in-breath and out-breath, come together with sight, come together with hearing, O king Soma. Whatever of thee was torn asunder — let that come together again; may our path-companions know us at the meeting-place of ways.

sanskrit: ahāḥ śarīraṃ payasā sam ety anyoanyo bhavati varṇo asya | tasmai ta indo haviṣā vidhema vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām ||
english: The days come together in his body with milk; one and another becomes the hue thereof. For him — thee, O Indu — do we offer worship with oblation; may we be lords of riches.

sanskrit: abhi kṣaranti juhvo ghṛtena- -aṅgā parūṃṣi tava vardhayantīḥ | tasmai te soma nama id vaṣaṭ ca- -upa no rājan sukṛte hvayasva ||
english: The sacrificial ladles flow over thee with ghee, nourishing thy limbs and joints. To thee, O Soma, reverence indeed, and vaṣaṭ! — call us in that good deed, O king.
